plain: To hold and use power or control

webster.text: To use with full command or power, as a thing not too heavy for the holder; to manage; as, to wield a sword; to wield the scepter.

more.text: To use or employ with the hand.
To handle; in an ironical sense.

example.quote: Numbers in both houses have turned about, and expected to wield us round with them, but they have been disappointed, and ever will be.
